workflow_runs.name: falsification
workflow_runs.display_title: Run each workflow before a merge or after it, never both

head_commit.message:
ci: status badges describe the last merge into main, not the last run

GitHub's workflow badges show the newest run of a workflow on ANY
branch. For the merge-gate lanes that means a contributor's failing
pull request reddens the README while main is perfectly healthy, and a
green badge is not a claim about main at all.

badges.yml now resolves the real thing after each merge, without
re-running anything: the merge commit names the pull request it came
from, that pull request's head commit carries the runs that decided the
merge was allowed, and their conclusions become the badges. Re-running
the lanes post-merge would also work and is what the split just
removed; this gets the same answer from checks that already ran.

Verified against live data rather than assumed. Replaying the step over
PR #41's head reports all five lanes passing; over bda4405 (the timing
flake) it reports tests-linux failing and the rest passing; over a SHA
with no runs it reports "did not run" in grey for every lane. That last
case is the one worth having -- a bypassed merge, a skipped lane, or a
workflow that quietly stopped triggering renders grey, never green.

On a direct push there is no pull request to resolve, so the status
files are simply not rewritten and the badges keep describing the last
real merge: an absence of information is not a change of state.

The scheduled lanes keep GitHub's badges, because containerAcceptance
and freshImageBuild genuinely run on main on a timer, so "latest run"
is main's state.

testReadmeDoesNotUseGitHubStatusBadgesForMergeGates fails if a
merge-gate lane drifts back to the built-in badge -- the two forms look
identical in a diff and mean different things.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
